summary: Recent M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY with embedded firmware experience in bare-metal C and C++ on ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers (MCU), FreeRTOS, and UART/I2C/SPI peripherals. Built interrupt-driven, deterministic firmware and debugged hardware-software integration across STM32, Arduino, Raspberry Pi, and NVIDIA Jetson platforms.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.
Used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and hardware-software integration end-to-end.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 MCU firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display, achieving 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination on STM32; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override; YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson sent control commands to the STM32 over UART.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) across a Jetson + Arduino controller.
Implemented two-link IK on Arduino in C++ driving five servos; integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors over a TCA9548A I2C mux for range-gated, contact-aware grasping (gripper close at 25 mm).
Deployed the Jetson-side arm bridge as a systemd service (auto-restart with backoff, non-root isolation, environment-file config) with static IP networking for reliable multi-device registration.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
